instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon unsalted butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, cumin powder, coriander powder, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the sauce thickens slightly.

instructions.title: Blend the Makhani Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is optional but highly recommended for restaurant-style smoothness.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir in the sugar and adjust salt to taste. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and cook for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the sauce.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 1 tablespoon of unsalted butter until melted and well combined. Crush the fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi) between your palms and sprinkle them into the curry. Simmer for just 2-3 minutes more; do not boil after adding cream. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a drizzle of extra cream before serving hot with basmati rice or naan bread.

tips: For a truly rich and authentic flavor, ensure your tomatoes are ripe and sweet. Using canned crushed tomatoes can also provide consistent results.
Do not boil the curry vigorously after adding the heavy cream, as it can curdle. Simmer gently on low heat.
To achieve a smoother sauce, blanch fresh tomatoes, peel them, and then puree before adding to the sauce. Soaking cashews beforehand also helps in achieving a creamy texture.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: A Timeless Indian Lunch Recipe

There are few dishes in the vast tapestry of Indian cuisine that evoke such widespread adoration as Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, with its rich, creamy tomato gravy and succulent pieces of chicken, has captivated palates worldwide. More than just a meal, Butter Chicken represents comfort, celebration, and the exquisite balance of flavors that define Indian cooking. Perfect for a hearty lunch, it's a dish that satisfies deeply, offering a luxurious experience whether you're dining out or enjoying a homemade version. If you're looking to bring the authentic taste of India to your midday meal, mastering this classic is an absolute must.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter" – a name that hints at the dish's indulgent nature. Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, it's a relatively modern invention compared to many ancient Indian recipes. The story goes that Kundan Lal Gujral, the founder of Moti Mahal restaurant, created the dish by simmering leftover tandoori chicken in a rich tomato and butter-based gravy. The result was a revelation: a mild, creamy, slightly sweet, and tangy curry that quickly became a sensation.

At its heart, Butter Chicken features tender pieces of chicken, traditionally marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried. These chicken pieces are then bathed in a velvety sauce made from tomatoes, butter, cream, and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, coriander, and fenugreek (kasoori methi). The generous use of butter and cream gives the sauce its signature richness and smooth texture, while the tomatoes provide a pleasant tanginess. It's renowned for its balanced flavor profile, making it approachable for those new to Indian food while still deeply satisfying for connoisseurs.

## Ingredients for Butter Chicken

Creating authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key components, divided between the chicken marinade and the luscious sauce.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 large ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashew nuts, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes (for richness and thickness)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or cashew cream for a dairy-free option)
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, to balance tanginess)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh coriander leaves, for garnish

## How to Make Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Step-by-Step

Making this beloved Indian lunch dish at home is surprisingly straightforward. Follow these steps for a truly delicious Butter Chicken.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a grill pan, heavy-bottomed skillet, or oven broiler. Cook the marinated chicken pieces until they are nicely charred and cooked through. If using a skillet, cook in batches to avoid overcrowding, ensuring a good sear. Set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt butter with oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Add Spices and Tomatoes:** Stir in the red chili powder, ground coriander, turmeric, garam masala, and cumin. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until aromatic. Immediately add the crushed tomatoes (or tomato puree). Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down.

5.  **Create the Creamy Base:** While the tomatoes are cooking, drain the soaked cashews and blend them with a little water (about 1/4 cup) until you have a smooth, creamy paste. Once the tomato mixture has cooked, remove it from the heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender) and blend until perfectly smooth. For an extra silky sauce, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot.

6.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the smooth sauce to the pot over low heat. Stir in the cashew paste, heavy cream, kasoori methi, sugar, and salt. Mix well. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce and simmer gently for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Do not boil, as this can curdle the cream. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

7.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and an optional swirl of cream before serving.

## Expert Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few insider tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse it with flavor, making a significant difference to the final taste and texture.
*   **Charred Chicken:** For authentic flavor, try to get some char on your chicken. Whether grilling, broiling, or pan-frying, a slightly smoky, browned exterior adds depth that distinguishes great Butter Chicken.
*   **Smooth Sauce:** Blending the sauce until absolutely smooth is crucial for that luxurious, velvety texture. Straining it through a sieve after blending ensures no lumps remain.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their unique aroma and slightly bitter, sweet, and tangy notes.
*   **Balance Flavors:** The beauty of Butter Chicken lies in its balance. Don't be afraid to adjust the sugar and salt to achieve the perfect sweet-tangy equilibrium. A pinch more sugar can cut through the acidity of the tomatoes if needed.
*   **Good Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality crushed tomatoes or ripe, sweet fresh tomatoes. They form the backbone of the sauce.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments.

*   **Naan Bread:** The undisputed champion pairing. Garlic naan, butter naan, or plain naan are perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera (cumin) rice provides a fluffy canvas for the creamy curry.
*   **Roti or Chapati:** For a lighter option, whole wheat roti or chapati also work wonderfully.
*   **Side Salad/Raita:** A simple cucumber and onion salad or a cooling raita (yogurt dip) can offer a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Pickle/Papadum:** A small side of Indian pickle or a crispy papadum can add an extra layer of texture and flavor.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect, you can adapt it to suit dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, chickpeas, or mixed vegetables for a delicious vegetarian version. Follow the same marination and cooking steps, adjusting for the ingredient.
*   **Dairy-Free:** Use a plant-based yogurt for the marinade and coconut cream or a cashew cream (cashews blended with water) instead of heavy cream in the sauce. Ensure your butter substitute is also dairy-free.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder. For less heat, use Kashmiri chili powder which provides color but minimal spice. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you don't have a grill, a quick trick is to place a small, heat-proof bowl with a burning charcoal piece in the pot with the finished chicken, drizzle a teaspoon of oil over it, and quickly cover for a few minutes. This infuses a smoky aroma.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I make Butter Chicken ahead of time?**
A: Absolutely! Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.

**Q: Is Butter Chicken spicy?**
A: Traditional Butter Chicken is generally mild, with a balanced sweet and tangy flavor. The spice level can be adjusted to your preference by modifying the amount of chili powder.

**Q: Can I freeze Butter Chicken?**
A: Yes, it freezes well. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer to a freezer-safe container. It can be frozen for up to 2-3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or cream if needed.

**Q: What kind of chicken is best for Murgh Makhani?**
A: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs are often preferred as they remain more tender and moist than chicken breasts, especially when simmered in the sauce. However, chicken breast can also be used.

**Q: Why is my Butter Chicken sauce not smooth?**
A: The key to a smooth sauce is thorough blending. Ensure your cashews are fully blended and that the tomato-onion base is also pureed until completely smooth. Straining the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve after blending can eliminate any remaining fibrous bits.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just an Indian lunch recipe; it's a culinary journey into the heart of comfort food. Its rich history, harmonious blend of spices, and utterly delicious flavor make it a perennial favorite. Whether you're an experienced cook or new to Indian cuisine, this guide provides everything you need to create a truly memorable meal. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your senses with this timeless classic.
